title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' following La Longue Marche. Grothendieck works with 2x2 matrices rho, sigma in GL2 (over a base scheme S). They satisfy the 'loop' relation rho*sigma^{-1} = -eps_1, where eps_1 = 1 + N_1 is unipotent and N_1^2 = 0 (eq. (33)/(35) on the previous page). He also sets N_0 = rho^{-1} N_1 rho = sigma^{-1} N_1 sigma and eps_0 = 1 + N_0. The previous page fixes a normal form: rho = (0 1; v w) and sigma = (0 -1; -v 1-w), so that rho + sigma = (0 0; 0 1) is an idempotent (37, 37bis).

Completing the computation. From -(1+N_1)sigma = rho one gets N_1 sigma = (0 0; 0 -1). Using sigma^{-1} = ((w-1)/v, -1/v; -1, 0), this gives N_1 = (0 0; 1 0), so eps_1 = (1 0; 1 1) is lower unipotent. Then rho^{-1} = (-w/v, 1/v; 1, 0) and N_1 rho = (0 0; 0 1), which give
(39) N_0 = (0 1/v; 0 0) and eps_0 = (1 1/v; 0 1),
in agreement with the relation u = alpha*v announced on page 301.

Marginal NB (39bis). sigma^{-1} rho = sigma^{-1}(rho sigma^{-1}) sigma = sigma^{-1}(-eps_1) sigma = -eps_0. Here eps_1 is conjugated by sigma^{-1}. A direct check gives sigma^{-1} rho = (-1, -1/v; 0, -1) = -eps_0. So the two 'local monodromies' rho and sigma differ by a unipotent eps_0, conjugate to eps_1.

Main text. With these normalizations he returns to the proposition of (original) p. 436. The scheme of 'twisted commutator' solutions was first to be written with a parameter gamma, as [alpha,rho] = [beta,·] eps_1(gamma). He decides instead to use mu = gamma + 1, which has a 'particularly remarkable significance', and keeps the factor eps_1(mu-1). Here eps_1(t) = (1 0; t 1). With xi = (A B; C D), the quantity P(xi) of formula (47) becomes simply P(xi) = D (40).

Check of what follows on the next page.
- The conditions are det = 1, xi = eta*eps_1(mu-1), Tr(xi rho) = Tr rho and Tr(eta sigma) = Tr sigma.
- Tr(xi rho) = vB + C + wD = w.
- Tr(xi eps_1(1-mu) sigma) = D - w - D(1-mu) must equal 1 - w. This forces D*mu = 1, i.e. mu = 1/D, with D invertible.
- So the solution scheme projects isomorphically to {xi : det xi = 1, Tr xi rho = Tr rho, D invertible}.
- It is then identified with the affine ('ax+b') Borel group B'_0 = {(mu lambda; 0 1)}.

Purpose. This explicitly describes a torsor / isomorphism u -> ([u,rho],[u,sigma],det u) for SL2/GL2 'loop-equation' data attached to genus-0 monodromy with unipotent local monodromy. These are rank-2 representations of the fundamental group of a punctured sphere, in a character-variety-like setting relevant to the Galois–Teichmüller programme.
errors: No mathematical error found. The computations of N_0, eps_0, sigma^{-1}rho = -eps_0 and (via the next page) mu = 1/D all check out.
The notation 'sigma^{-1}(eps_1)' in the margin means conjugation of eps_1 by sigma^{-1}, not multiplication. This is consistent with N_1 = sigma N_0 sigma^{-1}.

The text writes '[alpha,rho] = [beta,rho] eps_1(gamma)'. Given (41) on the next page, where xi and eta pair with rho and sigma respectively, the second bracket should probably involve sigma. This is a likely slip of the pen or a misreading.

ideas.what: Normal form for a pair (rho, sigma) in GL2 whose 'quotient' rho*sigma^{-1} is minus a unipotent. Under it rho + sigma is a rank-1 idempotent and the nilpotents N_0, N_1 become explicit upper and lower nilpotents.
ideas.modern_name: normal form of rank-2 local systems on a punctured P^1 with unipotent monodromy (explicit character-variety coordinates)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Fricke–Klein trace coordinates); modern character-variety literature

ideas.what: Reparametrization of the unipotent factor by mu = gamma + 1 so that mu = 1/D. Solutions of the twisted-commutator/trace system are identified with the affine Borel group {(mu lambda; 0 1)}.
ideas.modern_name: explicit torsor under the ax+b group for solutions of a commutator/trace equation in SL2

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit matrix computation inside a longer unpublished calculation. The results are correct but elementary normalizations; nothing here is a standalone new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The boxed marginal formula (39 bis) reads sigma^{-1}rho = -eps_0 (the minus sign was rewritten over a struck symbol), not '[-eps_0-] eps_0'.
'page 436' is Grothendieck's own internal pagination, and 'forme H' is uncertain. 'P(xi)' in (40) is written P(ξ).
